# Direct b-bit OPH backend benchmark contract

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

> **Historical artifact:** This records pre-hardening design evidence and does not define the current production method. See `docs/SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md` and ADR 0004.

Schema version: `backend-v1`

This contract is frozen before the backend/hash benchmark is run. A result may not be
removed because it is unfavorable. Any change to fixtures, references, scoring,
timing boundaries, or acceptance gates requires a new schema version.

## Decision under test

The production sketch candidate is undensified, fixed-register, one-permutation
MinHash built directly from every valid canonical k-mer in each represented interval.
The matrix kernel uses bit-sliced b-bit register comparison, 32-bit winner
verification, HLL cardinalities, and maximum directed containment. Minmers are not an
input to this candidate.

Three interchangeable hash streams are tested with otherwise identical OPH code:

1. `packed_fmix64`: the current rolling two-bit canonical encoding followed by the
   MurmurHash3 `fmix64` avalanche finalizer and public seed 42.
2. `nthash2`: the official ntHash2 split-rotation canonical rolling hash with its
   published nucleotide seeds.
3. `mashmap_murmur3`: MashMap-compatible `MurmurHash3_x64_128`, seed 42, applied to
   both ASCII strands with the smaller hash selected.

The ntHash2 implementation is pinned by vectors generated from official source commit
`c26bd4572a19de81e30d55042dbd33c1fd21d4b6`.

## Fixtures and cells

The full deterministic Phase 0 corpus remains required: identity, 0.1%, 5%, and 10%
substitution, 5% indel, coordinate offset, central inversion, reverse complement,
low-complexity blocks, tandem repeats, and unrelated sequence. This contract adds:

* deterministic ambiguity blocks;
* sparse valid islands surrounded by ambiguity;
* alternating high- and low-complexity intervals;
* unequal-length axes with an explicit padded suffix.

Every window-window cell is scored. Aggregate statistics may not omit zero-similarity,
repeat-rich, sparse-evidence, off-diagonal, or padded cells. A cell with exact k-mer
evidence must produce an estimate; a cell without exact evidence must remain missing.

The default synthetic run uses 262,144-base sequences, a 32 by 32 matrix, `k=21`,
14 comparison bits, a 32-bit verification fingerprint, and HLL precision 12. The
complete CHM13 chromosome 1 browser run and the chr1 higher-order alpha-satellite
sample remain required real-data checks.

## Accuracy tiers

The following register counts are measured independently; a tier is exposed only if
it passes its own gates:

| Tier | Registers |
| --- | ---: |
| Fast | 512 |
| Balanced | 1,024 |
| High | 2,048 |
| Maximum | 4,096 |

## References

Each candidate cell is compared with:

1. Exact distinct canonical k-mer sets using the specified maximum-containment score.
2. MashMap-compatible coordinated bottom-s sketches using the pinned MashMap
   MurmurHash3 implementation.

MashMap is an approximation reference, not a bit-for-bit expected result.

## Acceptance gates

For every exposed tier and every fixture:

* false-missing cells: zero;
* false-present cells: zero;
* mean absolute ANI error against exact sets: at most 0.015;
* 95th-percentile absolute ANI error against exact sets: at most 0.035;
* maximum absolute ANI error against exact sets: at most 0.060;
* expected forward/reverse diagonal cells: no direction inversions;
* unrelated cells: no estimate above exact ANI by more than 0.060.

The report also retains error against the MashMap reference and every maximum-cell
outlier. A hash backend is rejected for a systematic context-specific failure even if
its aggregate error passes.

## Performance and hash-quality measurements

For each hash backend the report records:

* valid k-mers hashed per second in a hash-only pass;
* complete axis-sketch construction time;
* complete matrix time after one warm-up;
* estimated owned bytes;
* register occupancy and 32-bit collision counts;
* native release performance;
* release Wasm performance in Chromium on the same machine.

Hash-only timing excludes FASTA parsing, allocation of the input sequence, exact and
MashMap oracle construction, matrix comparison, file I/O, and report formatting.
Axis construction includes hashing, OPH/HLL insertion, half-bin summary construction,
merging, and bit-sliced encoding. Identical input, tier, and scoring parameters are
used for all three hash backends.

## Selection rule

Correctness gates are applied before performance ranking. Among passing hash backends,
the default is the one with the lowest reproducible end-to-end Wasm axis-build time;
hash-only throughput is diagnostic and cannot override a slower complete build. The
backend, seed/constants, default tier, comparison bits, verification width, HLL
precision, and exact-k-mer transition rule are then recorded in an ADR and the
scientific specification.
